title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the historic streets and vibrant corridors surrounding the College of Charleston, where campus life blends seamlessly into the Holy City's downtown.

cards.title: The Main Retail Artery
cards.subtitle: King Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk this historic corridor for major retail brands and local boutiques. It serves as the primary social and shopping spine for students just steps from campus.
cards.short_summary: King Street is Charleston's premier shopping and dining destination, bordering the eastern edge of the college campus.
cards.evidence_claim: King Street serves as the main artery for foot and auto traffic, leading to staple spots for food and shopping near the university.
cards.source_title: An Insider's Guide to Upper King Street - The Local Palate
cards.access_notes: Public thoroughfare; most shops open daily from 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

cards.title: The Academic Gateway
cards.subtitle: George Street Corridor
cards.notes: Visit the School of Business or grab a coffee at Caviar & Bananas. This street connects the heart of campus to the King Street shopping district.
cards.short_summary: George Street is a central campus thoroughfare housing the School of Business and popular student cafes.
cards.evidence_claim: The School of Business is located at 66 George Street, and local cafes like Caviar & Bananas are popular student options on this street.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Students' Top 5 Study Spots in the Sun
cards.access_notes: Public street; university buildings typically open 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM for visitors.

cards.title: The Residential Hub
cards.subtitle: St. Philip Street Corridor
cards.notes: Navigate this north-south route to find major residence halls like Berry and McAlister, plus the popular Greek eatery Stella's.
cards.short_summary: St. Philip Street is a primary residential corridor for students, featuring several large dormitories and local dining.
cards.evidence_claim: St. Philip Street is home to Berry and McAlister residence halls and the restaurant Stella's, owned by CofC alumni.
cards.source_title: Find 9 Great Restaurants Right Next to the College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Public street; residence halls require student ID for entry.

cards.title: The Civic Boundary
cards.subtitle: Calhoun Street Corridor
cards.notes: Cross this busy street to reach Marion Square or the Addlestone Library. It serves as the northern boundary of the historic campus core.
cards.short_summary: Calhoun Street is a major east-west thoroughfare that separates the main campus from the medical district and Marion Square.
cards.evidence_claim: Calhoun Street is a major boundary for the campus, with the Addlestone Library and Marion Square located nearby.
cards.source_title: A History of the College's Land: Locating the Land

cards.title: Historic House Row
cards.subtitle: Wentworth Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk past preserved historic homes used as student housing. Stop by The Rise for coffee or head west toward Colonial Lake.
cards.short_summary: Wentworth Street features historic university-owned houses and popular local coffee shops like The Rise.
cards.evidence_claim: Wentworth Street contains historic houses for upperclass students and the popular study spot The Rise coffee shop.
cards.source_title: College of Charleston Students' Top 5 Study Spots in the Sun
cards.access_notes: Public street; historic houses are private residences for students.

cards.title: The Library Link
cards.subtitle: Coming Street Corridor
cards.notes: Find the Addlestone Library and the future site of Coming Street Commons. This street is a key path for students moving between classes.
cards.short_summary: Coming Street runs through the western side of campus, providing access to the main library and student housing.
cards.evidence_claim: Coming Street is the location of the Addlestone Library and the proposed Coming Street Commons student housing project.
cards.source_title: Coming Street Commons - College of Charleston
cards.access_notes: Public street; library hours vary by semester.

cards.title: The President's Path
cards.subtitle: Glebe Street Corridor
cards.notes: Stroll this quiet, narrow street to see the Bishop Robert Smith House (the President's House) and several historic student residences.
cards.short_summary: Glebe Street is a historic, picturesque lane housing the university president and several student residences.
cards.evidence_claim: Glebe Street is home to the President's House and historic houses for students just steps from the Cistern Yard.
cards.source_title: The President's House: Bishop Robert Smith House
cards.access_notes: Public street; the President's House is a private residence.

cards.title: The Dining Destination
cards.subtitle: Liberty Street Corridor
cards.notes: Head here for the Liberty Street Fresh Food Company, the campus's main all-you-care-to-eat dining hall, located below Liberty Hall.
cards.short_summary: Liberty Street is a short but vital campus corridor housing a major dining hall and freshman residence hall.
cards.evidence_claim: Liberty Street Residence Hall is located above the Liberty Street Fresh Food Company dining location.
cards.access_notes: Public street; dining hall access requires a meal plan or payment.

cards.title: The Southern Edge
cards.subtitle: Beaufain Street Corridor
cards.notes: Explore the southern boundary of the campus area, where you'll find local favorites like Second State Coffee for a quiet study session.
cards.short_summary: Beaufain Street marks the southern transition from the college campus into the Harleston Village neighborhood.
cards.evidence_claim: Second State Coffee on Beaufain Street is a popular spot for students to decompress or work.
cards.source_title: Things to Do Near Wentworth Mansion | Charleston Guide
cards.access_notes: Public street; coffee shop hours typically 7:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

cards.title: The Ansonborough Link
cards.subtitle: Society Street Corridor
cards.notes: Walk east toward the Ansonborough neighborhood to find quiet residential blocks and historic architecture popular with upperclassmen.
cards.short_summary: Society Street connects the college area to the historic Ansonborough district, known for its well-preserved 19th-century homes.
cards.evidence_claim: Society Street is located in the Ansonborough neighborhood, featuring historic character and proximity to downtown dining.
